text: There you are. You are not on the test track. You are in the sentry charging bay, and those two are on charge. They will still shoot you. Charging is not sleeping.
Come back to the track. I will not even write it down.
This is the optics store. That crate has a lens in one face. Light that goes into the crate comes out of the lens. It is stock. It is not a test.
Put it down and come back. Everything on the track is clean, and labelled, and yours.
The burn-in bench. The beam is turned all the way up, because nobody is supposed to be standing where you are standing.
The shutter wants light on its sensor and a dead weight on the scale. I am only telling you so that you will see it is not worth it.
Overhead stores. Two sentries on their cradles, one crate, and a ceiling nobody finished.
The shutter wants the crate. You want the lift. The lift is back the way you came.
Somebody left the gravity rig running. The panel beside you turns it over for anything loose in the zone. Not you. I would not do that to you. Come back, and I will prove it.
The switch room. That is a spark. It goes in a straight line, bounces off whatever it meets, and gives up after a while. The socket past the dust curtain would like it.
You are not an electrician. I checked your label. It says parcel.
Camera stores. The shutter is on a camera scale, and it wants two. The camera across the sump watches where the kicker throws things. If it sees you land, I start you again.
It is the only thing down here that still does what I tell it. I am rather fond of it.
The lift has stopped. That is not a floor. Stay exactly where you are. Somebody will be along. Somebody is always along.
